detail: In November 2013 Petrov said he had the budget for DTM; Mercedes signed him and Wolff named the Russian market as a reason. No sponsor or figure named.
Deal announced at a press conference at Russia 2 TV headquarters in Moscow.
ORLEN Deutschland became main sponsor of a new privately run BMW M4 for Kubica. No figure given.
First driver of the new WRT customer team; team boss said the programme was difficult to put together. No backing reported.
Second WRT seat filled with Audi's help after a Lausitzring test. No money mentioned.
Rookie in the privately run Aston Martin team. Not WRT in 2019. No backing reported.
WRT added a third Audi for him. No backing or figure reported.
Late call up after Ed Jones could not travel; father Adrian Newey spoke with Gerhard Berger about the seat. No money mentioned.
Placed by the Mercedes junior programme after winning the 2012 F3 Euro Series. Astana link was only his 2010 F3 team. Only Wikipedia found.
Mercedes junior driver in the Thomas Sabo car; Thomas Sabo is a Mercedes DTM partner, not his personal sponsor.
Son of Ricardo Gelael whose family company holds the KFC Indonesia franchise; KFC brand Jagonya Ayam backed his own team from 2014. 2013 backing not documented. Mostly Wikipedia.
KFC Indonesia committed to support Tim Jagonya Ayam with Carlin in FR3.5 and F3.
Father Michael Latifi founded Sofina Foods and funded his career. No 2013 figure found.
Son of former Minardi test driver and real estate developer Chanoch Nissany. No source says how his racing was funded. Only Wikipedia.
Later profiles list Colombian backers Escudería Telmex, Claro and Coldeportes; start year of these deals not confirmed.
Nissan GT Academy graduate; Nissan funded programme, not a pay driver. GP3 with Arden came in 2014.
Mercedes engined F3 driver; DTM test as a reward at end of 2014, Mercedes reserve later. No personal funding reported.
Named a BMW DTM driver at the BMW end of year event; team named on 13 January 2014.
BMW test driver promoted to race seat with da Costa; team named on 13 January 2014.
Moved from MTEK to RMG in the BMW team shuffle.
Moved to Schnitzer alongside Bruno Spengler.
Left DTM for the Rahal Letterman Lanigan BMW team in the United SportsCar Championship.
Left DTM to focus on endurance racing with the Z4 GT3.
Audi signed him to replace Filipe Albuquerque.
Moved to the Audi LMP and GT programme.
Returned to DTM after losing his Force India F1 seat.
Swapped from Rosberg to Abt in the Audi team allocation.
Moved from Abt to Rosberg.
Moved to Abt alongside Ekström, Tambay and Mortara.
Left Abt after seven seasons to join Rockenfeller at Phoenix.
Signed by Mercedes; team allocation to Mücke confirmed on 8 April 2014.
Lost his race seat and stayed as test and reserve driver.
Confirmed in the seven car line-up on 5 March 2014; moved from Mücke to the fifth HWA car on 8 April 2014.
